articles.headline: Yahoo Fantasy Football Expert League Recap: Playoff-picture shakeup as top teams collide in Week 9
keyFacts: Yahoo Fantasy Football Expert League Week 9 featured matchups between all six top teams in playoff position, shaking up the standings.
Loeb defeated first-place Pianowski 125.56 to 117.18, while Boone defeated Winks and Edholm defeated Harmon.
Waiver wire activity will be busy following multiple injuries to key players, including Michael Wilson and Puka Nacua.
body: If you're unfamiliar with the Yahoo Fantasy Football Expert League , let's fill you in a bit before we go over Week 9. Yahoo Fantasy houses some of the leading analysts in the industry, and we were fortunate enough to get all of them in a league for the 2026 NFL season. To keep you up to date on things, we'll be providing weekly recaps on all the action. Let's get into it.
Here's a look at the standings at the midway point of the fantasy season:
Here's a look at the Yahoo expert league standings after Week 9.

We had some big-time matchups in Week 9 that could alter the playoff picture in the expert league. All six teams in playoff position faced off against each other last week — Harmon versus Edholm, Pianowski versus Loeb and Boone versus Winks. That shifted the standings quite a bit at the top, so let's get into it.

The most notable matchup was between first-place Pianowski and Loeb, which came down to the two prime-time games between the Bears and Bucs on SNF, and Vikings and Bills on MNF. With Colston Loveland and Luther Burden III, Pianowski had a chance to distance himself from Loeb, creating a cushion to potentially withstand Josh Allen going off. Burden and Loveland combined for 24.6 points, but Loeb was able to muster 28 fantasy points from the Bears D/ST and Rome Odunze, giving Allen an easy path to close it out. While the Bills QB only had 13.86 fantasy points, it was enough to lift Loeb to a 125.56-117.18 victory.
The Onesies have done it again. pic.twitter.com/6R7QEjNR7E
— Max Loeb (@loebsleads) November 10, 2026

Pianowski wasn't able to secure the win despite a 36-point explosion from QB Jordan Love, whom he regretted not pairing with one of his receivers. Check out more of Pianowski's key draft mistakes as we hit the midseason mark here .

The other key matchup was between Boone and Winks, two formidable teams. But after going on a five-game winning streak, Winks has now dropped back-to-back games. Boone, on the other hand, started the season with a tie and loss, but has since won six of the past seven games.
I peaked early. It's over.
— Hayden Winks (@HaydenWinks) November 10, 2026

Boone used a big performance from Christian Watson and Cam Little while the injury to Josh Jacobs, plus down games from Justin Jefferson and Jaxon Smith-Njigba really sunk Winks. Boone has one of the deeper rosters in the Expert League and is well-positioned to compete for a title as the playoffs approach.

The final bout between top teams was Harmon against Edholm, who entered Week 9 as one of the hottest teams in the Expert League on a three-game winning streak. He used big games from Joe Burrow and Puka Nacua to get by Harmon, but both sides suffered tough losses on the injury front. Harmon won't have Michael Wilson the rest of the way while Edholm could be without Nacua for what seems like at least four games.
It will be an interesting week on the waiver wire in this league with multiple injuries and the trade deadline having produced a few fantasy-relevant deals .

A quick shoutout to Joel Smyth and Josh Norris, who both picked up wins as the high scorers of the week. Each is positioned to compete for a playoff spot, creeping up on Harmon in sixth place. Let's also not forget Ray Garvin and Eric Froton, each at 3-6 and not out of it yet.

articles.headline: Best value bets for UFC 334: Ciryl Gane vs. Josh Hokit
keyFacts: UFC 334 at Madison Square Garden features two title bouts and primarily features strikers instead of one-trick grapplers.
Fightnomics analysis identifies Ciryl Gane as the heavyweight favorite against Josh Hokit due to Gane's technical counter-striking and size advantage.
Fightnomics also highlights Chris Duncan and Charles Radtke as favored bets for their respective matches on the event card.
body: In sharp contrast to the last numbered event , UFC 334 in New York at Madison Square Garden features two title bouts and is loaded with good strikers and fewer one-trick grapplers . Those who do wrestle at above-average pace are generally also good strikers. So we should see plenty of matchups being decided on the feet.
Let’s break down some key spots on the card:
Ciryl Gane (-210) vs. Josh Hokit (+185)
(Fightnomics)

The profiles are similar, though the size and pedigree are very different for this heavyweight title bout. It’s two of the more accurate heavyweight strikers, yet ones who aren’t all about power. Though Hokit is definitely more likely to initiate takedowns, we should still see some extended exchanges on the feet.

The key differences are size and pace. Hokit averages over twice the striking output while standing compared to Gane, however it’s largely driven by a barnburner against Curtis Blaydes and a drubbing of Derrick Lewis, That said, his strength of schedule against technical strikers is not at Gane’s level, and Hokit will be noticeably undersized at range.

Gane is carefully measured, keeps his distance and lands accurately while staying away from trouble. Hokit’s aggressive forward style leads to landing a lot of strikes, but also absorbing far more than is typical — especially at heavyweight — with a generally poor head-strike defense metric.

How Hokit’s aggression plays out will determine the outcome. Delivering as much output as he’s capable of doing would surely win rounds and possibly set up a ground finish. But Gane appears specifically suited to forcing a slower fight and making overly aggressive moves pay dearly with technical counter-striking. It’s been a fast rise for Hokit, but the model still likes the champ as the two-to-one favorite, and that assumes Gane can fight effectively in reverse with his counters.
Best bet: Gane to win
Chris Duncan(-160) vs. Drew Dober (+135)
(Fightnomics)

Dober nearly always gets involved in a slobberknocker, and the numbers reveal the telltale signs: prefers to stay standing, uses a high-striking output, scores lots of knockdowns but actually gets hit more often than he lands. He might have a willing dance partner in Duncan, who exhibits some of the same tendencies but minus the power or damage absorbed. At a minimum, that makes Duncan the younger, bigger and less damaged fighter of the two, which generally translates into success in a shootout.

Duncan can also fall back on his ground game. Dober’s takedown defense rates about average, and if Duncan commits he could sway otherwise close rounds. He’s also shown an ability to maintain or increase output in his most recent decision victories. That stamina will be necessary to hang with Dober, who invites a wild pace. Together, these advantages give a playable edge to Duncan at a price that should remain affordable.
Best bet: Duncan to win
Stephen Thompson (-150) vs. Charles Radtke (+120)
(Fightnomics)

This will be Wonderboy’s farewell appearance, and it might have been more fitting to pair him with striker. But in this matchup, despite some decent striking metrics for Radtke, I expect he will deploy the game plan of heavy wrestling that he used in his last two wins.

Wonderboy is no stranger to opponents wanting to close the distance, though over his career his takedown defense is still just barely above average. Should Radtke get frustrated chasing the notoriously evasive Thompson, we could see this turn into a contest of ground control, starting with fence line clinching. A glance at my Strikers vs. Grappler graph reveals they are on opposite sides of stylistic tendencies, where historically I tend to favor the wrestler.

Radtke's two knockouts suffered drop his chin rating well into the red, normally a big risk facing a rangy striking specialist. But further context reveals those came against two of the division’s best in Mike Malott and new title contender Carlos Prates. So not exactly a knock against Radtke’s durability.
Best bet: Radtke to win at plus money

articles.headline: NFL trade deadline 2026: Vikings reunite with Kirk Cousins; Colts stick with Taylor; 49ers get WR Allen – live reaction
keyFacts: The Minnesota Vikings acquired quarterback Kirk Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders in exchange for a 2027 third-round draft pick.
The San Francisco 49ers acquired wide receiver Keenan Allen from the Indianapolis Colts in exchange for a 2027 sixth-round draft pick.
The Buffalo Bills acquired safety Amani Hooker from the Tennessee Titans in exchange for a 2027 second-round pick and a 2027 fifth-rounder.
body: Odell Beckham Jr’s latest stint on an NFL active roster has proved to be brief. The Minnesota Vikings have released the veteran wide receiver just one day after promoting him to their 53-man squad ahead of Monday night’s prime-time game against the Buffalo Bills.

Beckham played in the game but was not targeted. His departure is not expected to be permanent, however, with Minnesota planning to re-sign him to their practice squad, according to Tom Pelissero of the Ringer.
The move comes amid a busy week of roster changes in Minnesota, highlighted by the deadline-day acquisition of quarterback Kirk Cousins from Las Vegas.

The NFL trade deadline has come and gone, bringing an end to a busy period of roster reshuffling across the league. Seventeen trades were completed during the season, including Kirk Cousins’ return to Minnesota, Josh Downs’ move to Kansas City and a flurry of activity involving the Jacksonville Jaguars.
Teams can no longer complete trades until the new league year begins at 4pm ET on 11 March 2027, although deals can be agreed in principle before then.

Another important wrinkle: from now until the end of the season, every player whose contract is terminated must pass through waivers, regardless of veteran status. That means even established veterans cannot immediately choose their next destination if released.

Correction: that’s 18 trades after last-minute deal sending Atlanta Falcons center Ryan Neuzil to the Baltimore Ravens in exchange for offensive lineman Andrew Vorhees and a sixth-round pick in the 2028 draft.

Not a trade, but the 1-7 Dolphins are placing quarterback Malik Willis on injured reserve with a groin injury that has developed into a core muscle problem, according to multiple reports. Willis had been playing through the injury, which limited his mobility, but an MRI revealed that the condition now requires an extended period of rest. The injury is not considered season-ending, although Willis will be sidelined for at least four weeks.
The Colts have decided against trading their star running back ahead of Tuesday’s deadline despite receiving offers from multiple teams, according to Tom Pelissero of the Ringer.
Several suitors were prepared to part with a second-round draft pick and additional compensation, but Indianapolis demanded a blockbuster package to even consider moving Taylor.

The decision comes amid a roster overhaul following the dismissal of general manager Chris Ballard. The Colts have already traded receivers Keenan Allen and Josh Downs, but Taylor and quarterback Daniel Jones are expected to remain in Indianapolis.

The Kansas City Chiefs have landed wide receiver Josh Downs and a 2027 seventh-round pick from the Indianapolis Colts in exchange for fourth- and fifth-round selections in the same draft, according to multiple reports.

Downs, a former third-round pick out of North Carolina, gives Patrick Mahomes another reliable target in the passing game. The move continues a busy deadline day for Indianapolis, who have also sent veteran receiver Keenan Allen to the San Francisco 49ers.

The Denver Broncos have acquired linebacker Daiyan Henley from their AFC West rivals, the Los Angeles Chargers, in exchange for a fourth-round pick in the 2027 draft and a fifth-rounder in 2028, according to multiple reports.

Henley, a former third-round pick out of Washington State, has developed into one of the NFL’s most promising young linebackers. The move strengthens Denver’s defense as they look to create separation from a logjam of teams atop the AFC standings, where the top six teams are within a game of the No 1 seed.

The Broncos expect to receive a fourth-round compensatory pick in 2027 for the departure of defensive lineman John Franklin-Myers, allowing them to part with their own fourth-round selection in the deal, according to Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer.

Kirk Cousins’ return to Minnesota comes with an unusual statistical wrinkle. The veteran quarterback has played through the first part of the season without a week off in Las Vegas, but the Vikings have already enjoyed their bye. That scheduling quirk means Cousins could theoretically start 18 regular-season games – a first in NFL history for a quarterback – if he takes over immediately and remains under center for the rest of the season. You like that?

A total of 19 players in NFL history have appeared in at least 18 regular-season games in a single year, and none have been quarterbacks, according to Josh Dubow of the Associated Press. Fifteen achieved the feat between 1925 and 1930, while four have done so since the league adopted a 17-game schedule in 2021: Leonard Williams (2023), Mike Williams (2024), Rashid Shaheed (2025) and Dre’Mont Jones (2025).
Cousins rejoins Vikings as Raiders launch Mendoza era

Kirk Cousins is heading back to Minnesota. The Vikings have acquired the veteran quarterback from the Las Vegas Raiders in a blockbuster exchange for a third-round pick in the 2027 draft, according to multiple reports, including ESPN’s Adam Schefter and NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport.
The move reunites Cousins with the franchise where he spent six seasons from 2018 to 2023 and gives Minnesota an experienced option under center as they look to salvage their season.

For Las Vegas, the trade clears the way for No 1 overall draft pick Fernando Mendoza to take over as starting quarterback. The Raiders, who sit at 4-5, will throw the rookie straight into the deep end, with his first two NFL starts coming against two of the league’s toughest defenses in Seattle and Denver.

Tennessee are building quite the war chest. The Titans now hold two first-round picks and two second-round picks in the 2027 draft, plus another two first-rounders in 2028. That gives them six picks in the first two rounds over the next two years and a golden opportunity to reshape their roster.

The 7-1 Bills were in need of safety help and it appears they’ve gotten it. Buffalo have acquired safety Amani Hooker from the Tennessee Titans, according to Tom Pelissero of the Ringer, bolstering their secondary amid their push for the AFC’s top seed.
Hooker, 28, is the NFL’s joint-interceptions leader this year and has established himself as one of the league’s most versatile safeties.
Buffalo are sending back a second-round pick in the 2027 draft to Tennessee in exchange for Hooker and a 2027 fifth-rounder, according to reports.

The 49ers are sending a sixth-round pick in the 2027 draft to Indianapolis in exchange for Allen, according to reports. With San Francisco getting healthier at wide receiver, the 34-year-old provides experienced depth at a relatively modest price.

The San Francisco 49ers have acquired six-time Pro Bowl wide receiver Keenan Allen from the Indianapolis Colts, according to multiple reports, giving Brock Purdy another experienced target for the stretch run.

Allen, who had been seeking a move to a contender, joins a San Francisco team with inside track on the No 1 seed looking to bolster their passing attack ahead of the playoff push. The 34-year-old veteran brings more than a decade of NFL experience and one of the league’s most reliable pairs of hands. Terms of the deal have yet to emerge.
The NFL reinstated Brandon Aiyuk on Monday and gave the 49ers a two-week roster exemption to determine their next step with the disgruntled former All-Pro wide receiver.
Aiyuk had been on the reserve/left squad list since December 2025, when he stopped reporting to the Niners while rehabbing a knee injury.

It doesn’t sound like Aiyuk will be making any return to San Francisco – coach Kyle Shanahan said on Monday that the status change “means absolutely nothing to our team” – and they could attempt to trade him before today’s deadline. Will teams want to sign him given the fact that he hasn’t played a game since December 2024, and even during that season, he had just 374 receiving yards in seven games? The league also told Aiyuk and the players union last week that it believes he must repay the Niners $13m in already-paid bonuses for failing to participate in team activities.

His agent, Drew Rosenhaus, seems to believe a team will take the chance. On the Pat McAfee Show today, he said: “I think that in all likelihood Brandon will probably sign with a team that knows him, somebody that has somehow been affiliated with him either in college or the 49ers. That’s just my guess.”
The Falcons are signing kicker Jake Moody off the Ravens’ practice squad and releasing fellow Nick Folk, according to insider Jordan Schultz.

Moody had a 53-yard field goal and an extra point in his debut for the Ravens last Thursday. Folk, a 19-year veteran of the league, missed his fifth field-goal attempt of the season in Atlanta’s loss to the Bengals in Madrid on Sunday.
Who are the Vikings’ options on the quarterback market?

They have the best defense in the NFL and an excellent group of position players, headlined by wide receiver Justin Jefferson. A competent quarterback could be the difference between wasted windows and Super Bowl contention. Some of the names being thrown around:
Eagles-Bengals trade for DE Arnold Ebikeite falls through

With just under four hours until the deadline, we’ve gone from one trade on the day to minus-1. NFL insiders Ian Rapoport and Jordan Schultz report that the Bengals’ trade with the Eagles for Arnold Ebikeite has been called off.

Rapoport says it was scratched by the Bengals “with an eye toward keeping a future compensatory draft pick they would’ve lost with this deal” and that the agreement had not been finalized. That compensatory draft pick would have been the one the Bengals were to receive for former edge rusher Trey Hendrickson signing with Baltimore this year in free agency.
The Jaguars have reportedly received calls about wideout Brian Thomas Jr, but ESPN says they have told teams they aren’t interested and have no plans to trade him.

Thomas was the 23rd overall pick in the 2024 draft and had a breakout season as a rookie, with 87 catches for 1,282 yards and 10 touchdowns plus Pro Bowl honors. His production has dramatically dropped since: he has 10 catches for 117 yards and two touchdowns. He received zero targets from Jacksonville quarterback Trevor Lawrence in Thursday’s loss to the Ravens.
Not a trade, but an NFL development nonetheless: Dolphins defensive tackle Zach Sieler will undergo season-ending surgery on his ruptured biceps, per ESPN.
Sieler was hurt during Miami’s loss to the Lions. He had recorded 24 tackles and two sacks in eight games this season.
The Dolphins are 1-7 and stuck at the bottom of the AFC East standings. Sieler’s absence leaves a hole in their defensive line.

Jordon Hudson is suing two Airbnb hosts over a Ring doorbell camera video of a shirtless Bill Belichick. Hudson says that the 2023 clip invaded her privacy by prompting public disclosure of her relationship with the former Patriots coach.

The Lions strengthened their depleted secondary on Monday, trading for Jets safety Andre Cisco in exchange for a 2028 sixth-round pick. Cisco has played in nine games this season for New York but wasn’t a regular starter. Detroit are down two safeties in star Kerby Joseph, who is out with a knee injury, and Thomas Harper, who is on injured reserve.

I’m sure you’ll hear more on this topic later today from the Guardian’s resident Philadelphian Bryan Armen Graham, but for now! After trading Arnold Ebiketie to the Bengals, the Eagles now up to 10 owned picks in the 2027 draft.
Philadelphia are in the middle of a seven-game losing streak, the franchise’s worst skid since 2012. General manager Howie Roseman is stocking up.
The Colts have had a busy few weeks. After a 2-4 start, they fired longtime GM Chris Ballard. They traded eight-time All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner.

The big question is how much that fire sale continues today. There’s speculation Indianapolis could trade away star running back Jonathan Taylor or quarterback Daniel Jones – or even the both of them.

Several insiders around the NFL have said Taylor would command a high package – perhaps similar to what Christian McCaffrey went for when he was traded from the Panthers to the 49ers in 2022 for a second-, third- and fourth-round pick in the 2023 draft, plus a fifth-round pick in 2024. The Giants have been floated as a potential landing spot, but it’s unclear if they could give the Colts what they want.
The Eagles are still making moves, trading edge rusher Arnold Ebiketie to the Bengals for a 2027 sixth-round pick, per multiple reports.
A second-round pick by Atlanta in 2022, Ebiketie has 16.5 sacks in his career. He spent four seasons with the Falcons and then joined the Eagles this offseason on a one-year, $7.3m contract.

A team to watch today: the Minnesota Vikings. If you watched them on Monday night, you’ll know about their messy quarterback situation. Regular starter Kyler Murray is out with a hamstring injury; Carson Wentz, the 33-year-old veteran backup, was dreadful against the Bills, going 8-for-25 for 81 yards and three turnovers. His completion percentage was the worst by a quarterback with at least 10 attempts in a game this season.

Murray is considered week-to-week, but the offense has been mediocre even with him. Minnesota traded away JJ McCarthy, the player they had selected just two years ago with the No 10 overall pick, in September. The Vikings still have the NFL’s leading scoring defense, but their offense is an obvious weakness. After a 6-0 start, they have lost two straight.

Could a reunion with Kirk Cousins be in store? The 38-year-old is the starter for the Raiders, but they also have top draft pick Fernando Mendoza waiting in the wings. Do they try for Daniel Jones, who had a short stint as the Vikings’ third-stringer in 2024?
ESPN’s Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport report that the Vikings have begun making calls around the league about trading for a quarterback.

AFC South leaders Jacksonville went all-in on Monday, adding defensive tackles Jordan Davis in a blockbuster trade with Philadelphia. The Eagles got a 2027 first-round draft pick and a 2029 second-round pick in return.

Davis has just 1.5 sacks with one interception in nine games this season, but he had career highs in 2025 with 4.5 sacks and 72 tackles. He was a first-round draft pick in 2022 and helped the Eagles beat the Chiefs in Super Bowl LIX, receiving a three-year, $78m contact on the heels of that win.

Monday’s trade capped a trio of defensive moves by the Jaguars, who have won five of their last six games. They also traded for Falcons safety Jessie Bates III and for Saints defensive tackle Davon Godchaux.
In total, the Jaguars gave up six future draft picks. If the season ended today, they would be the No 3 seed in the AFC. They clearly think they can go higher.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of the 2026 NFL trade deadline. After weeks of splashy moves, swirling rumors and increasingly frantic speculation, we’re finally approaching the moment of truth. The clock is ticking and all 32 teams have until 4pm ET (9pm GMT) to get their affairs in order.

It’s already been an eventful trading season. The Chicago Bears made the biggest splash by acquiring All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons from the Tennessee Titans for a package including two first-round draft picks. The Jacksonville Jaguars made a trio of moves to bolster their defense, headlined by a trade with Philadelphia to land defensive tackle Jordan Davis. The Indianapolis Colts have been busy dismantling their roster, shipping eight-time Pro Bowl guard Quenton Nelson to Seattle and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to San Francisco. Meanwhile, Marvin Harrison Jr has landed in Houston, Joey Porter Jr has joined Dallas and the injury-ravaged Baltimore Ravens have brought in veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett.

But plenty of questions remain unanswered. Will Indianapolis continue their fire sale by parting with star running back Jonathan Taylor? Which contenders will make one last push for reinforcements? And could another blockbuster deal emerge before the window slams shut?
We’ll be following every confirmed trade, credible rumor and last-minute development throughout the day, with instant analysis of what the moves mean for the playoff race and beyond.
Strap in. Deadline day has arrived and there’s plenty still to play out.

articles.headline: How to get the crude lockpick recipe in DREADMOOR, all lockpick types, and how to use them
keyFacts: Players can obtain the Crude Lockpick recipe in DREADMOOR by completing the Catch a Mutant Fish Story Quest from Mad Nick.
Crafting the Crude Lockpick requires one rubber and one metal plate, and players can store up to twelve in their inventory.
Players pick locks in DREADMOOR by positioning the lockpick on the sweet spot and holding the D key to turn it.
body: Although brute force can take you far in DREADMOOR , having a lockpick at hand is a requirement if you wish to get past locked doors and access treasure chests across the game’s many settlements.
But getting the tool means first acquiring its recipe, something only doable a few hours in. Here’s how to get the first lockpick recipe in DREADMOOR and how the mechanic works.
Table of contents
How to get the crude lockpick recipe in DREADMOOR How to pick locks in DREADMOOR
All DREADMOOR advanced lockpicks, explained
How to get the crude lockpick recipe in DREADMOOR

You can unlock the Crude Lockpick recipe in DREADMOOR as a reward by completing the Catch a Mutant Fish Story Quest. The quest is unlocked after meeting Mad Nick on his island and requires catching two Cryptmaw fish.

The fish can be found in the locations below, but only late at night. You will also need to have at least 30 Line Strength to attempt the catch, so don’t forget to equip the Braided Line to your fishing rod at the trading post to meet the requirements.

Screenshot by Destructoid After returning to Mad Nick and unlocking the recipe, you will be able to craft the Crude Lockpick by using 1x Rubber and 1x Metal Plate. You can have a maximum of twelve in your inventory. Just don’t forget, they will share slots with First Aid Kits.
Screenshot by Destructoid Read what’s behind the latest news in gaming (with a bit of snark) by subscribing to the Destructoid Checkpoint newsletter !
How to pick locks in DREADMOOR

You can pick locks in DREADMOOR by first using your mouse to position your lockpick and find the sweet spot within the lock, marked by a glowing light. Now, hold D to turn the lock while keeping the tool in the right position to unlock it. Forcing the lock will cause your lockpick to break.
Screenshot by Destructoid All DREADMOOR advanced lockpicks, explained

Apart from the Crude Lockpick, you can unlock two other variants in DREADMOOR : the standard iron Lockpick and the Master Lockpick. Both are clear upgrades and can be crafted after unlocking their respective recipes.

Item Recipe In-Game Description Lockpick TBA An iron lockpick made by someone who knows the craft. Reliable enough in skilled hands and able to open most known locks. Master Lockpick TBA A true work of thieving art, forged from tempered alloy. It glides like silk, yet remains strong and reliable. We will be adding more to the above once we unlock the recipes for the advanced lockpicks. In the meantime, don’t forget to check out all Fishing Rods and how they work in DREADMOOR .

body: Oura announced its quarterly earnings today and said it agreed to acquire Counsel Health for $625 million, after adding the company’s AI chatbot to its app earlier this year. Counsel Health calls itself an “AI-native primary care company,” using the app to deliver AI-generated responses and insights based on users’ health data reported from their wearables that can then proceed to a conversation with one of its in-house physicians.
Oura is acquiring medical AI chatbot startup Counsel Health
Doctor visits could start with a readout of your Oura ring data.
Oura says it expects the deal to close before the end of the year.

Oura CEO Tom Hale said in an interview with Bloomberg that the acquisition is part of a plan to connect wearables, clinical AI, and access to doctors based on insights from biometric data to answer questions or monitor ongoing conditions. Counsel Health’s AI chatbot can connect Oura users to a real doctor directly from the app and draw on users’ biometric data from their wearables in its answers to medical questions. The plan they describe in the press release is to focus on three areas, including preventative care, acute care for episodic health concerns, and specialty and chronic care for things like reproductive and cardiometabolic health.

According to Bloomberg, Counsel Health’s CEO Muthu Alagappan says it’s also planning to expand its network of on-demand physicians, which is currently “made up of about 50 people.” Counsel’s 70 employees will join Oura as part of the deal, with Alagappan becoming Oura’s chief clinical AI officer. Oura says in its announcement that Counsel will also continue offering its medical AI platform outside of Oura’s user base through new and existing enterprise partners, including “health plans, health systems, consumer health organizations, and employers.”

articles.headline: Vikings strike up blockbuster trade to reunite with $333m QB and put Super Bowl path back on track
keyFacts: The Minnesota Vikings traded a 2027 third-round pick to the Las Vegas Raiders to reacquire quarterback Kirk Cousins.
Vikings general manager Nolan Teasley secured the trade before the deadline to address offensive struggles and support an injured roster.
Cousins returns to Minnesota where he played from 2018 to 2023, aiming to keep the 6-2 team competitive for the Super Bowl.
body: The Minnesota Vikings have struck a deal with the Las Vegas Raiders to bring back quarterback Kirk Cousins.

After their dismal Monday Night Football showing against the Buffalo Bills , in which their issues on offense was exposed, the Vikings had no choice but to enter the market and seek a trade for a quarterback.
Cousins was traded at the deadline to the Vikings Getty
And their saviour is a familiar face, with the Vikings waiting until the eleventh hour of the NFL trade deadline to secure a reunion.
Vikings general manager Nolan Teasley was able to get a deal over the line with the Raiders to land veteran signal caller Kirk Cousins .
All it took to reunite with their former franchise star was a 2027 third-round pick.
It’s a homecoming of sorts for the 38-year-old Cousins, who was the Vikings’ star quarterback from 2018 until 2023.
In his first spell in Minnesota, he completed 67.9 per cent of his passes for 23,265 passing yards and 171 touchdowns to just 55 interceptions.
He then left as a free agent in 2024 for the Atlanta Falcons , before switching to the Raiders last year.
Vikings revert back to familiarity with Cousins return
For the Vikings, the trade is a small price to pay to salvage their season.

Sitting at 6-2 on the year but with an injured Kyler Murray , a veteran back-up in Carson Wentz who is coming off a historically poor performance, as well as inexperienced third-string Max Brosmer, SKOL nation knew they were at risk of their season going terribly wrong.
Their defense alone has shown that they are capable of winning a Super Bowl , ranking second in the league in total yards allowed per game with 280.0.
They also rank first in the league in points allowed with 14.5 per game.
Cousins spent six seasons in Minnesota from 2018-2023 AP
Justin Jefferson’s numbers could be boosted thanks to a reunion with Cousins Getty
However, it has been a completely different story on the other side of the ball.
The offense has been virtually a non-starter , ranking 31st in the NFL in total passing yards on the season and passing yards per game with 1,286 yards total bringing their average to 160.8 per game.
Only the Tampa Bay Buccaneers have put up fewer – recording 1,277 total passing yards for an average of 141.9 yards per game.
The difference is their defense hasn’t been able to be as much of a contributory factor to help them win games, made clear by their 3-6 record.
Cousins’ trade not only brings some stability at the quarterback position, but also keeps superstar wide receiver Justin Jefferson content amid recent frustrations .
Jefferson enjoyed his finest season in 2022 while playing with Cousins, setting career bests with 128 catches and 1,809 yards, which both led the NFL.
Mendoza will now take over the reins in Las Vegas Getty
The receiver is sure to welcome Cousins back, who, in nine outings for the Raiders this season, completed 64.1 per cent of his passes for 2,340 yards and 20 touchdowns to just eight interceptions.
Only Joe Burrow of the Cincinnati Bengals has found his receivers in the end zone on more occasions (23 touchdowns).

Head coach Kevin O’Connell and the Vikings get a proven veteran under center in Cousins – who has earned over $333m in his 15-year career, and will now hope this move keeps them competitive in the NFC in their pursuit of Super Bowl LXI.

From the Raiders’ perspective, though, they only had to pay the 38-year-old a total of $650,000 for nine games and over six months serving as a mentor to No. 1 overall NFL Draft pick Fernando Mendoza .
They also got draft capital, showing that the trade could be a win-win for both parties.
Now, the former Indiana Hoosiers star’s era in the Sin City will get underway with all that knowledge and learnings from one of the league’s most consistent quarterbacks.

articles.headline: Florida AG subpoenas DSA over potential illegal funding from Cuba and China
keyFacts: Florida AG James Uthmeier issued a subpoena to the Democratic Socialists of America to investigate potential illegal funding from Cuba and China.
The subpoena demands documents about DSA delegations to China and Cuba to determine whether state trade laws were violated, Uthmeier said.
Fox News Digital reached out to the DSA for comment, but Uthmeier did not detail specific criminal allegations or name individuals.
body: Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier announced Tuesday that his office has issued an investigative subpoena to the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) to investigate whether the organization accepted contributions from "foreign sources of concern," including entities in Cuba and China.

"Our laws prohibit accepting contributions from foreign sources of concern," Uthmeier said in a video statement. "We will not allow foreign adversaries to influence Florida through the backdoor of non-private fundraising."

The subpoena demands documents related to recent DSA delegations to China and Cuba, where organization members met with Cuban government officials, to determine if the DSA violated Florida's Deceptive and Unfair Trade Practices Act, according to Uthmeier.
DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS OF AMERICA ACTIVISTS SIGNED PLEDGE TO SUPPORT, DEFEND 'CHINESE SOCIALISM'
Uthmeier did not detail specific criminal allegations or name individuals accused of violating state law.
The DSA has repeatedly praised the Cuban regime and routinely advocates for lifting American sanctions and ending the U.S. embargo against Havana.

The organization has sent multiple delegations to Cuba in recent years. During a 2023 trip, DSA members met privately with Cuban President Miguel Díaz-Canel and sought to establish formal communication channels with government ministries, according to a State Department report released in July.
The legal action comes shortly after several DSA-backed candidates won races across federal, state, and local levels in last week's elections.
Fox News Digital reached out to the DSA for comment.

articles.headline: Brooklyn Courtnall, daughter of NHL veteran Russ, is back home with San Diego
keyFacts: Bay FC loaned defender Brooklyn Courtnall to San Diego Wave FC for the remainder of the 2026 NWSL season.
The move allows Courtnall to train on her childhood field and enables her family to attend her games in person.
Courtnall also became the first female soccer player to partner with the California-based activewear brand Vuori.
body: Playing professional soccer in Southern California has turned into a homecoming for Brooklyn Courtnall. The defender, 23, is in her second professional season and has returned to familiar ground after Bay FC loaned her to San Diego Wave FC for the rest of the 2026 NWSL season.

One part of the move stands out. Courtnall is now training on the same field where she played as a young player growing up. Being back in the region also means her family can come watch her games in person, and that is something she values a great deal.
Brooklyn Courtnall

Courtnall starred at USC, where she earned All America honors, and she has already played international soccer for Canada. Sports run deep in her family. Her father, Russ Courtnall, played in the NHL and also represented Canada on the international stage. Her own time with the Canadian national team continues a family tradition that started with him.

Her career is now growing away from the field as well. Courtnall has become the first female soccer player to partner with Vuori, the California activewear company. The deal connects a Southern California athlete with a brand based in the same state.

Courtnall wears Vuori when she is away from training and matches, and she enjoys trying out different items from the company’s collection. She has not made an appearance on behalf of the brand yet. She is looking forward to the opportunities the partnership could bring in the future.

The deal shows how business opportunities are expanding for players in women’s soccer. For Courtnall, the main reason she loves her job is simple. She gets to play soccer every day, and she has turned the game she loved as a kid into her profession.
Now that she is back where her soccer journey started, Courtnall is building her professional career while staying close to the reasons she fell for the sport in the first place.

articles.headline: You Can Play GTA 6 On A 13-Year-Old Xbox And It’ll Run At The Same Framerate As PS5 Pro
keyFacts: Microsoft announced that Grand Theft Auto 6 will be playable on day one via Xbox Cloud Gaming on the 13-year-old Xbox One.
Players using Xbox Cloud Gaming on an Xbox One will experience the game running at Xbox Series S graphics settings and a targeted 30fps framerate.
To play the game this way, users need a digital copy of the game and access to Xbox Cloud Gaming through a subscription or separate pricing.
body: Grand Theft Auto 6 is only coming to PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S at launch, but that doesn’t mean those consoles will be the only places to play it. Technically, fans who are still on Xbox One, which came out back in 2013, will also have a shot at exploring Rockstar Games’ latest version of Vice City thanks to Xbox Cloud Gaming.

Microsoft revealed the surprise last-gen perk in an update to its cloud gaming program this week. “Grand Theft Auto VI will be playable on day one through Xbox Cloud Gaming on Xbox One and Xbox Series X|S, starting at 1am ET,” the company announced. “That means more players can experience one of the most anticipated games of the year on the consoles they already own. The game uses Xbox Series S graphics settings when cloud-streamed with Xbox Cloud Gaming.”

Series S graphics settings include the game running at a targeted 30fps framerate, the same as what will be available to players on Xbox Series X and PS5, as well as PS5 Pro. Sony’s more powerful hardware will still give players access to improved image quality with PSSR, but the game won’t run at 60fps anywhere, at least not at launch.

So what do you need in order to play GTA 6 on an Xbox One? Well, you’ll still need to own a digital copy of the game, which costs $80 and began pre-loading this week. You’ll also need access to Xbox Cloud Gaming, either via a Game Pass subscription or via Ã la carte pricing. Ten hours of cloud gaming time in Vice City will cost Xbox owners $4.

What you won’t be able to do is stream GTA 6 to a mobile device or PC. Those options, which are a standard part of the rest of Xbox Cloud Gaming’s offerings, are excluded from the streaming agreement with Rockstar. It’s unclear if that’s a functionality that may be added sometime down the road after the game has been out for a while. GTA 6 will also support remote play on both Xbox and PS5, meaning you can stream it to other screens locally, including the PS Portal.

“Weâre excited to bring Grand Theft Auto 6 to more Xbox players at launch, and we will also be adding more titles from Rockstar Games to Xbox Cloud Gaming including Grand Theft Auto 5, Red Dead Redemption 2, and more in the coming months,” Microsoft added in today’s announcement.

I have no idea how many Xbox Ones are still out in the wild, or how many people may be tempted to blow the dust off of them instead of upgrading to a current-gen console. But given the ongoing price hikes for both the PS5 and Xbox Series X/S, it’s a really nice option for those who can’t otherwise afford to buy new hardware this fall for GTA 6.

articles.headline: Sony have cancelled Fairgame$, once again reminding us that chasing live service big bucks basically never works
keyFacts: Sony has cancelled the live service game Fairgame$ developed by Haven Studios, according to a report by Bloomberg.
Haven Studios executives Sean Decker and John Doyle stated that player feedback and retention fell short of goals.
Sony announced that the studio will shift its focus to collaborating with other PlayStation Studios teams without job cuts.
body: You know, I'm sure that Sony had every intention of following through on their intention to release 10 live service games by 2026, as they mentioned way back in 2022. Well, as far as an intention that's designed to please shareholders can go, anyway. And now here we are, almost five years on from that comment that continues to haunt them with the news Fairgame$ has been cancelled.

This comes from a report from Bloomberg, who shared that, thankfully, there are no planned job cuts due to the game being cancelled. In a statement, Sony said that, "The studio will shift its focus to collaborating with other development teams across PlayStation Studios, while also exploring new creative opportunities, though didn't go into detail as to who those other teams are.

Bloomberg were also privy to a note shared with developers at Haven Studios from executives Sean Decker and John Doyle that follows a recent test of the game: "While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set. Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game."

Sony have, notably, failed to capitalise on the live service trend; I'm sure I don't need to remind you about Concord. Hell, this isn't even taking the end of Destiny 2 into consideration, once a driving force of live service games, or how Marathon has struggled to pick up an audience in the way that Sony may want it to. You just can't force a game to be popular, especially in a genre like shooters.

For those that either missed or forgot about Fairgame$, it was announced back in 2023 and was supposed to be a "competitive modern heist game where you team up to break into exotic locations and steal the cargo," all while taking on security and other, real people. Gameplay was never formally revealed, only a CGI trailer, and was set to come to PC as well as PlayStation. Bloomberg also noted that the game had been reworked multiple times since the announcement and was set to be re-revealed with a new name. Ultimately, it looks like Katharine was a little generous with her timeline of six months.

articles.headline: PlayStation Officially Cancels Live-service Shooter Fairgames
keyFacts: Sony canceled the live-service shooter Fairgames after Bloomberg reported that player feedback from a recent test fell short of expectations.
Haven Studios developers will not face layoffs and will instead support other Sony Interactive Entertainment-owned studios.
Sony decided to cancel the game due to mixed retention results and challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre.
body: Sony has canceled Fairgames (aka Fairgame$) three years after the live-service shooter was announced, Bloomberg reported on Tuesday. No one at its developer, Haven Studios, is getting laid off, and instead Haven will support other Sony Interactive Entertainment-owned studios, according to that report.

Farigames recently held a playtest and, according to an internal email reviewed by Bloomberg, feedback from that playtest didn't live up to PlayStation's expectations. "While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set," executives Sean Decker and John Doyle said in the email. With "challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre," Sony decided to cancel the game.

Fairgames reportedly had been reworked multiple times since its 2023 reveal. It would have been the debut game from Haven, which was founded in 2021 by former Assassin's Creed producer and Google Stadia Games and Entertainment head Jade Raymond, who has since left the studio. Haven was acquired by Sony in 2022.
Fairgames is Sony's latest live-service misfire

Back in 2022, Sony announced a huge push for live-service games, aiming to release at least 10 by 2026. While games like Helldivers 2 and Gran Turismo 7 have been steady live-service hits, Sony's push has largely failed. Concord is the most notable misfire, as it was actually released before Sony reversed course and shut it down shortly after launch in embarrassing fashion.

A live-service God of War game, a multiplayer The Last of Us game, and many others were canceled before they could see the light of day. PlayStation studios working on live-service games, including London Studios, Firewalk Studios, and Bluepoint Games, were all shut down in recent years. In June, Sony laid off most of the Destiny team at Bungie, as "Destiny 2 fell short of expectations" with players. Recently, Horizon Hunters Gathering was reportedly delayed so it can be rebooted in response to negative player feedback (which sounds not too dissimilar to the Fairgames situation).
And now, Fairgames has been canceled.

articles.headline: Meghan's father Thomas Markle detained for allegedly cutting off ankle monitor, officials say
keyFacts: Thomas Markle was detained in Florida for allegedly cutting off his court-ordered ankle monitor, according to justice department officials in Los Angeles.
A federal magistrate judge in Tampa ordered Markle jailed without bond, placing him in federal custody.
Markle faces one count of possessing indecent images of children after the FBI seized items from Los Angeles storage units.
body: - Published
Thomas Markle, the father of Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, has been detained in Florida for allegedly removing his ankle monitor, according to justice department officials in Los Angeles.

Markle appeared before a federal magistrate judge in the Florida city of Tampa after allegedly removing the monitor at 01:45 local time (06:45 GMT), a justice department (DoJ) spokesperson told the BBC.
The judge ordered him jailed without bond and he is now in federal custody, the spokesperson said.
Markle, who has previously denied possessing images of child sex abuse, was arrested in Florida last week and placed under house detention. He was also ordered to wear a location monitoring device.
The BBC has contacted his representatives.
US Judge Lindsay S Griffin said on Tuesday that Markle's housing situation "had become untenable", according to court documents.

Griffin cited a "lack of suitable housing", writing in the order that "no condition or combination of conditions would reasonably assure the safety of any other person or the community and the defendant's appearance in court".
He also ordered a medical evaluation for Markle and said he "must receive all necessary and prescribed medication unless discontinued by a physician".
"Release conditions are court orders, not suggestions," Bill Essayli, the US attorney for Central California, wrote on X on Tuesday about Markle's alleged removal of his ankle monitor.
"We will continue to prosecute this case to the fullest extent of the law," Essayli added.

Markle was first arrested last week after the FBI, acting on warrants, searched storage units in Los Angeles registered to him which he had rented since 2008, with the last payment being made in October this year, the DoJ said.
Inside the units the FBI says agents seized about 78 items, including film negatives, slides and books that they allege contained child sex abuse material.
Witnesses "positively identified" Markle in two of the images believed to contain child sex abuse material.
In those images, the man pictured "appears to be in the age range of 30s to 40s", which suggests the alleged abuse dates back decades as Markle is currently 82 years old.
Markle appeared in court last week following his arrest. No plea was taken during the appearance, which set several conditions for his pretrial release, including that he be kept in home detention.
He is charged with one count of possessing indecent images of children, according to the DoJ.
FBI director Kash Patel said last week that Markle "allegedly targeted innocent children and sought to steal their innocence through his criminal actions".
Markle has called the allegations "sick lies".
He moved to the Philippines last year after he had a series of strokes, and lived in Cebu until May. He was reportedly learning to walk again in Florida after having his leg amputated.
The duchess has been estranged from her father since 2018. The BBC understands she broke contact with him last year, telling him she and the authorities knew he had abused young girls.
In a previously shared statement, Meghan confirmed the existence of the letter and wrote: "I am deeply distressed... my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed."
She said she hoped it could be understood why she had largely cut off contact from her father and did "not allow him to have contact with our children".

articles.headline: What we know so far about Jensen Huang's affair with suspected Chinese spy
keyFacts: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted to being unfaithful to his wife with businesswoman Alice Huang, who US intelligence officials believe was a Chinese spy.
Nvidia has opened an independent investigation into the affair, while the FBI and congressional committees are also examining the situation.
Nvidia stated it does not believe US national security was compromised and that Jensen Huang remains committed to leading the company.
body: - Published
One of the Artificial Intelligence (AI) industry's most important figures has been accused of having an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.

US intelligence officials believed that Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, who had a close relationship with Nvidia CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang, was a spy for Beijing, according to a New York Times report.
Jensen Huang admitted, external to having been "unfaithful" to his wife and apologised for hurting her and their children.
US tech giant Nvidia, one of the most valuable companies in the world, has opened an independent investigation into the affair.
It said it does not believe US national security had been compromised - and added that Jensen Huang was committed to continuing to lead the company.
Here is what we know about the affair and why it matters.
Who is Alice Huang and what do we know about the affair?
US officials believed that Alice Huang had been recruited to spy by China's top intelligence agency, the New York Times reported, external. Her current whereabouts are unknown.

Alice Huang, who is of no relation to Jensen Huang, was a top executive at Singapore-based data centre firm Megaspeed between March and November 2023. The firm had been suspected of helping divert Nvidia chips to China, a concern that Nvidia maintains was investigated and debunked.

However, Megaspeed is under investigation by the Singapore government regarding previous allegations that the company was circumventing US sanctions on the export of Nvidia's high-end chips. The BBC has contacted Megaspeed for comment.
The company told the New York Times last month its current leadership took the allegations seriously and had appointed external legal advisers to conduct an internal investigation.
Surveillance reportedly revealed communications between Alice Huang and an American citizen, who was subsequently identified as Jensen Huang through a process known as "unmasking".
It remains unclear what, if any, intelligence Alice Huang â who is also known as Huang Le â allegedly gathered and passed to Beijing. She did not respond to the paper's request for comment.
When the BBC asked Nvidia if the company was aware of intelligence concerns, the company said it was not.
"We trust that if we were the target of a genuine threat, the US government would have notified us," an Nvidia spokesperson told the BBC.
China has rejected the spying allegations.
Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun told reporters: "The allegations about Chinese spies are entirely groundless, speculative and intended to smear and malign China."
The New York Times reported in late October that US President Donald Trump had been briefed last year on intelligence alleging Alice Huang was spying on China's behalf.
Asked by reporters on Sunday whether he wished he had "acted on the intelligence", Trump responded: "No, I don't think so. I think he's [Jensen Huang] an honourable guy."

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, meanwhile, refused to comment when asked about Jensen Huang. Last spring, the secretary of state reportedly oversaw the drafting of a memo that warned the Trump administration about Jensen Huang's relationship with the Chinese businesswoman.
Why does it matter?
Nvidia is at the heart of US and China's AI race, which is why the billionaire's affair has sparked national security fears among American lawmakers.
Trump has said "whoever wins AI wins", and the fear is that if China gains the upper hand in AI, it will supercharge the country's military and surveillance capabilities.

The US advantage is in large part because of US companies like Nvidia, working with producers like the Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC), which makes more than 90% of the world's most advanced chips.
Since 2022, the US has used various export controls to keep the top tech out of China, which it says helps retain America's competitive edge and protects its national security.

This means companies like Nvidia have been largely locked out of the world's most lucrative market, with Jensen Huang once saying that Nvidia's share of the Chinese market had gone from around 95% to effectively zero.
Huang has engaged in shuttle diplomacy between Washington and Beijing, hoping to find a US-approved way back in, and shaping US policy on China along the way.
Sunday's revelations may explain why Jensen Huang has failed to bring home the biggest prize of all to Nvidia: the Trump administration's blessing to sell all but its most advanced chips to China.
Who is Jensen Huang?

Born in Taiwan in 1963, Jensen Huang was nine years old when his family moved to the West Coast of the US. He graduated as an electrical engineer from Oregon State University, and then with a master's degree in the same field from Stanford University.

Jensen Huang then worked at US chip firm AMD before co-founding Nvidia. Known as "Daddy Huang" in Taiwan and once lauded as the "Taylor Swift of tech", he has a reputation as a workaholic and perfectionist with incredibly high standards for his staff.
He has an estimated fortune of $155bn (Â£115bn), according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index.

"Jensen Huang is a tech visionary of the likes of Steve Jobs," Stephen Witt, the author of Thinking Machine, a biography on the Jensen Huang, told the BBC, adding that he was responsible for creating AI hardware as we know it today.

The Nvidia co-founder has a famously close relationship with Trump. At the recent AI summit at the White House, where 42 tech executives were present, the president was flanked by Elon Musk and Jensen Huang.
Trump said he spoke with Jensen Huang on Monday and asked him "'Did you have any idea she was a spy?'"
"He said 'I had no idea she was a spy' and I really believe him," Trump told reporters.
What investigations are now under way?
Nvidia has launched an independent investigation into the affair and has hired New York law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to carry out the probe.
The investigation will be led by former US Attorney for New York's Southern District, Joon Kim.
US President Donald Trump said on Monday that the FBI was also investigating the affair. The FBI declined to comment further when contacted by the BBC.
Jensen Huang has also been asked to appear for a joint closed-door briefing for several Congressional committees on 18 November.
Members of the US House Foreign Affairs Committee asked the Nvidia chief executive to appear to explain his interactions with Alice Huang, as well as Nvidia's security protocols around espionage.
Jensen Huang has yet to say he will comply, a person familiar with the committee's demand told the BBC.
What is Nvidia and how important is it?
Founded by Jensen Huang and fellow electrical engineers Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem in 1993, the company was originally known for chips that process graphics, particularly for computer games.
Eventually it changed focus to AI, a field it now dominates.
Jensen Huang rescued Nvidia from bankruptcy on more than one occasion, and took risks on AI a long time before the rest of the world did, effectively building the infrastructure from scratch.

"Today when we think of that, we think of these giant data centres - none of that existed. There were no customers for the stuff he was building. In fact his first customer was Open AI at the time they had 30 people - he actually gave it to them, he donated it to them," Witt told the BBC.
Every notable tech company building AI tools and infrastructure, including Amazon, Meta, Google, and Microsoft, now use Nvidia chips.
Currently worth about $4tn, Nvidia is one of the most valuable companies in the world.
For now, the firm's board appears to have little appetite for removing Jensen Huang, saying in a statement on Sunday that they have "confidence in Jensen and his leadership team".
Sources tell the BBC his removal is unlikely because there is so much money at stake.

There is no public succession plan for the 63-year-old. He has often said he hopes to continue in the role for decades, and Bloomberg reports he has created an informal leadership structure around him unlike a traditional company's hierarchy.
His children, Spencer and Madison, and son-in-law Nico Caprez work at Nvidia in senior roles.
Who is Jensen Huang's wife?
Jensen Huang met his future wife Lori Mills at Oregon State University while studying electrical engineering in the early 1980s. The pair were lab partners.
They married in 1985, about eight years before he co-founded Nvidia, and have two children, Madison and Spencer.

In 2007, the couple founded the Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang Foundation. The charitable fund has seen its assets surge in recent years, driven by the soaring value of Nvidia shares, and is estimated to be worth more than $9bn.
Its donations include tens of millions of dollars to engineering programmes at Oregon State and Stanford University.
Witt told the BBC that Jensen Huang has gone to great lengths to present himself as a family man, adding: "That's very important to him".

"He praises his wife, he talks about her in very glowing ways," he added. "The fallout of this would be bad for anyone's family. But for someone who has gone to such great lengths to cultivate an image of being a family guy and who keeps his children very close, it is very bad."
Additional reporting by Tom McArthur in London, Ayeshea Perera and Tessa Wong in Singapore and Helen Davidson in Sydney

articles.headline: Tech cannibalization to become mainstream? Removing expensive components and reballing memory set to reach 7–9% of smartphones by 2027
keyFacts: TrendForce estimates that smartphones using reballed memory will increase from 3 to 4 percent in 2026 to 7 to 9 percent by 2027.
Rising mobile DRAM prices are driving smartphone manufacturers to reuse memory components to reduce production costs.
TrendForce expects memory price increases to accelerate in the first quarter of 2027, which could encourage companies to use reclaimed parts in costlier products.
body: - Reballed memory could account for up to 9% of smartphones in 2027
- Rising DRAM prices are pushing phone makers toward reused memory
- Budget handsets currently account for most smartphones using reballed chips
Rising memory costs are pushing smartphone manufacturers toward an unusual form of component reuse, with refurbished memory expected to appear in more devices by 2027.
TrendForce estimates this approach will account for 3–4% of smartphones in 2026, before its market penetration increases to approximately 7–9% next year.
The shift is being driven by expensive mobile DRAM, which is increasing manufacturing expenses and putting additional pressure on brands serving price-sensitive buyers.
Reused memory offers manufacturers a cheaper route
Reballed memory comes from integrated circuits removed from existing circuit boards, then prepared for another installation after their original solder connections are carefully replaced.
Those connections use small metal spheres beneath the chip, allowing it to communicate electrically with the board while occupying very little physical space.
During reballing, technicians clear away the existing solder, prepare the contact surface, and attach a fresh set of appropriately sized replacement solder spheres.
The component can then be fitted to another board, although its suitability depends on its condition, handling history, and the quality of the refurbishment process.

TrendForce says 4GB LPDDR4X currently makes up most of the reclaimed supply, with use concentrated in inexpensive 4G handsets costing under CNY 1,299 (~$195).
Buyers in this category are particularly sensitive to retail prices, giving manufacturers an incentive to recover usable parts rather than rely entirely on newly manufactured memory.
Using previously installed chips can reduce component expenditure and help brands limit price increases, especially when customers have little room for more expensive smartphone models.
Although reballed memory is currently concentrated in cheaper smartphones, rising DRAM prices could encourage manufacturers to introduce it into more expensive models.
Higher memory costs could extend the practice
TrendForce expects memory price increases to accelerate in Q1 2027, adding pressure to manufacturers already managing expensive production.
That environment could encourage companies to consider older or lower specification parts in more costly products.
Even with faster adoption, reclaimed memory is expected to represent a small proportion of the total LPDRAM consumed by smartphones annually.
Consequently, its growing presence is unlikely to reverse the upward movement in contract prices, since its contribution to total memory demand remains limited.

The financial attraction also comes with technical concerns, particularly when manufacturers cannot establish consistent quality across components obtained from different suppliers and refurbishment channels.
Repeated heating can place stress on electronic packages, while damaged contacts or imperfect replacement work may affect electrical performance after installation inside smartphones.
Traditional reballing relies on heating solder until it melts, and component makers generally advise limiting devices to no more than three such heating cycles.

Laser-based methods can concentrate heat around solder contacts instead of warming the entire package, potentially reducing thermal exposure during component refurbishment and subsequent installation.
Manufacturers therefore face a choice between immediate savings and possible costs arising from failures, repairs, warranty claims, or dissatisfied customers over extended periods.

articles.headline: Bungie drops gameplay trailer for Marathon's 'co-op PvE roguelite' mode and swanky new social space
keyFacts: Bungie announced the Symbiosis update for Marathon, releasing on December 8 with a permanent co-op PvE roguelite mode named Expedition.
The update also introduces a social space called Limbo, a Team Deathmatch beta, a new map area, and a sword-wielding runner shell named Bishop.
Bungie stated that the update rollout will coincide with a fully free-to-play open play week where player progress and items will carry over.
body: Bungie has served up our first proper look at Marathon's big Symbiosis update, which is set to go live on December 8 with a permanent PvE mode, plus an all-new Team Deathmatch mode and a social space called Limbo.

Symbiosis represents the start of "the evolution of Marathon," Bungie said, with "a plethora of updates and changes" to the game. First and foremost is the addition of Marathon's PvE mode, now permanent and with a new name, Expedition, that's described in the teaser as a "co-op PvE roguelite." Details beyond that haven't been revealed just yet, but Bungie called it "phase one" of the team's PvE plan, suggesting that it remains a work in progress.

Also notable in Symbiosis is the addition of Limbo, a "social space" where players can hang out without getting aired out (although there does appear to be a little area set aside for friendly shootin'), and its firing range, a handy way to test the game's guns without having to venture into its less friendly locales.

Speaking of which, the Perimeter map is being expanded with new points of interest and tunnels, and a new sword-wielding runner shell, Bishop, will debut with the update. For those who prefer the PvP life, the update will also kick off a beta for Marathon's Team Deathmatch mode.

Overall, Symbiosis looks to be a pretty big deal, and while today's tease is light on detail, the early reaction among players on Reddit and social media seems quite positive. Bishop is already racking up fans:

One other bit of good news: The rollout of Symbiosis on December 8 will also mark the start of an "open play week," during which the game will be fully free to play, including the new modes and content. If you dig it and decide to stick around (ie., buy the game), any progress and items earned will carry over.

articles.headline: Dot-eat? Google Introduces 3 More Top-Level Domain Names
keyFacts: Google publicly released three new top-level domain names ending in .eat, .fly and .here on Tuesday.
Google partnered with registrars to offer the domains to trademark holders before a wider public rollout.
A one-time early registration fee will disappear on Nov. 17, after which unused names can be registered at a fixed annual rate.
body: We’re trained to type .com almost on autopilot, but more top-level domains are coming. You’ll soon see websites ending in .eat, .fly and .here. It’s a new way for restaurants, travel agencies and other service providers to customize their online presence.
Google successfully filed these domain types with ICANN, the Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers, back in 2012, but only released the new registry options to the public on Tuesday.

There’s always a concern that someone will steal a business’ domain name, a process known as cybersquatting. To prevent new top-level domains from being registered and ransomed at high prices, Google’s partnered registrars offered .eat, .fly and .here websites to registered trademark holders ahead of a wider rollout. This closed access period lasted from Sept. 1 to Nov. 9.
More from CNET

Google’s blog post about the new domains revealed several big businesses that have already secured new web addresses during the trademark holder selloff. Wingstop bought up wingstop.eat, while agriculture and food-tech company Clayton Farms secured the america.eat address. Caddy, Canary and Voltair are some of the businesses with new .fly domains.

The most interesting assortment of companies have tied down .here addresses. In its blog, Google describes .here domains as denoting businesses “where people get things done.” They utilize fairly common words that people might search for. Real-estate app Zillow owns rent.here and sell.here, while bloodtest.here is owned by SiPhox Health, a home blood-testing service.
A number of Google-partnered registrars are now accepting registrations for the three new domain types.

There’s currently a one-time early registration fee associated with registering the new domain names, though it is diminishing and will completely disappear on Nov. 17. After that, any currently unused .eat, .fly and .here names can be registered and maintained at a fixed annual rate, just like any other type of domain.
A representative for Google didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.

President Donald Trump stated that a return to full-scale war with Iran is unlikely.
body: Rep.-elect Adam Hamawy (D-NJ) deflected a question on whether he considers Iran an adversary.
Hamawy said the United States “pushed” Iran into fighting when asked if Iran was an adversary in an interview on CNN’s Situation Room with Wolf Blitzer and Pamela Brown .
“I see that we are pushing Iran into a fight when we have the leverage to, kind of, bring them to the table,” Hamawy said Tuesday.

The Iran war was a top campaign point for Democrats during the midterm elections along with the affordability of rising gas prices and groceries. Democrats won the majority in both the House and Senate in the “bluenami” and have begun the groundwork to fulfill their agendas.
Hamawy said Iran and the U.S. have to step back from the war efforts. When pressed on whether Iran was the adversary, he said the U.S. was “making adversaries when we should be making friends.”

Brown pointed out that Iran has killed Americans, to which Hamawy responded, “and we’ve killed a lot of them as well.”

articles.headline: OpenAI acquires Odessia, travel startup created by Sonder founder
keyFacts: OpenAI acquired the AI travel startup Odessia, according to founder Francis Davidson, who is now working at OpenAI.
The financial terms of the acquisition were not disclosed, and Odessia's travel tool has already been shut down.
OpenAI did not publicly announce or confirm the acquisition, and has not yet detailed any new travel-specific plans.
body: OpenAI has acquired an AI travel agent called Odessia, according to Odessia’s founder, Francis Davidson. Davidson says in a post announcing the deal that he’s now working for OpenAI, helping the AI lab with the future of travel.

Terms of the deal were not disclosed, but this looks like an acqui-hire. Davidson’s announcement focused largely on how he built his AI travel agent Odessia by directing teams of AI agents. The year-old Odessia raised a $6 million pre-seed round led by Sequoia and launched its AI travel agent around five months ago. Davidson says that it had helped early adopters plan millions of dollars’ worth of travel, but the tool has already been shut down.

OpenAI did not announce this acquisition, nor confirm it to TechCrunch, when asked. Nor has it announced new travel-specific products or plans. It does, however, count such companies as Bookings.com, Expedia, and KAYAK as customers or partners.

Travel is one of the main areas that people are using personal AI assistants to help with. And, back in July 2025, when OpenAI launched its ChatGPT agent, it mentioned travel as one of its potential uses.

Acquiring Odessia is interesting for another reason. Davidson is well known in the travel industry after he founded a travel startup called Sonder as a college student in 2014. It was sort of like Airbnb, but it focused on leasing upscale apartments in major cities worldwide. The pandemic badly hurt it, and as it climbed out of that rut, it went public via a SPAC but didn’t raise as much money as it needed, Davidson later said in a post announcing his resignation as CEO in June 2025.

When a key partnership with Marriott fell through, the company went into bankruptcy and wound down. The bankruptcy trustee sold Sonder’s name, trademarks, and website domain in 2026 to TravelAI, and that website operates as a curated guide to the kind of travel rental properties that Sonder was once known for. Prior to its downfall, Davidson had built Sonder into a unicorn with $143 million in revenues. While Sonder was not, ultimately, a success story, Davidson is the kind of battle-scarred founder that Silicon Valley often values.
So we’ll have to wait and see what OpenAI has in store now, with his joining the company. OpenAI has not yet responded to a request for comment.

articles.headline: World of Warcraft Forever Hotfix Will Thin Out Overcrowded Zones and Help Faction Balance
keyFacts: Blizzard released a hotfix to lower player populations in overcrowded World of Warcraft Forever zones and address faction imbalances.
Community Manager Kaivax stated that Blizzard is throttling character creation for the more populous faction to achieve a 50/50 split.
Blizzard stated they will continue to monitor zone congestion and faction data to make further adjustments as necessary.
body: World of Warcraft Forever has been incredibly popular, and has gone down as the biggest WoW launch in history. It's little wonder, then, that some zones are absolutely packed with players — but thankfully, Blizzard has implemented a fix.

In a hotfix last night, Blizzard lowered the population in overcrowded zones, which should give players more of a chance to get quests done without competing with a hundred other players to tag a spider. In the developers' notes, Blizzard also noted that "We’ve made this an even bigger change on the PvP ruleset, following feedback from players that they felt overcrowded in several places. We will continue to monitor how zones feel and make further adjustments as necessary."

Unlike past versions of WoW, which had a variety of servers available, World of Warcraft Forever has one server that's divided into different rulesets: PvP, PvE, RPPvP, RP and Hardcore. Instead of dividing players among different servers, Blizzard uses layering to group people into different instances of the world. And because WoW Forever's whole thing is being surrounded by other players, Blizzard seemingly opted to try and get as many people into each layer as possible without causing problems.

However, while it's fun to see hundreds of players running around each zone, this approach has caused some issues. Some people on the PvE rulesets have reported difficulties in being able to finish quests, especially in the earlier zones, as they have to compete with dozens of different players to get anything done. But the problem is especially bad for players in the PvP rulesets because of a faction imbalance.

At least here in the US, The Horde is much more popular than The Alliance, and that's causing problems. For Alliance players, they're outnumbered when they're questing in the world, which means they get killed instantly in later zones. For Horde players, they can't create new toons, because Blizzard is throttling character creation to try and preserve faction balance.

Blizzard Community Manager Kaivax has addressed this in a seperate note last night, saying, "It’s vitally important that the PvP rulesets in WoW: Forever have balanced factions where both factions vie for supremacy, creating memories of epic victories and stunning defeats that we all remember for years to come. While even the most extreme case in a region is currently at roughly a 55/45 split, that is not as close as we want it to be." Blizzard wants to get that balance as close to 50/50 as possible.

To address the matter, Kaivax says, "In the short term, that means that it will become increasingly difficult to create characters on the more populous faction in each region – currently Horde on North American PvP rulesets or Alliance in EU Roleplay-PvP. As everyone settles and shifts, these may flip to the other side."

Despite some of these growing pains, though, World of Warcraft Forever is still proving to be one of the smoothest launches in Blizzard history. Launch night went off without a hitch, thanks to the servers running on around 251TB of RAM and over 70,000 CPU cores.

- Fixed an issue where Cooldown Manager wasn’t showing Seals correctly.

- Power Infusion will now correctly persist when used on allies.
